title: Introduce policy-rule autorouter spec & config validator
creator: Asha Patel
description: Define an explicit, machine-checkable specification for the routing 'autorouter' rules that compose region selection, customer tier routing, and fallback model variant declarations; implement a config validator that rejects ambiguous or unsafe rule combinations before deployment. This ticket covers spec, validator implementation, and CI gating to prevent bad configs from reaching runtime.
acceptance_criteria: A formal DSL grammar (BNF-style) exists for the autorouter rules and is checked in to docs/confluence with illustrative examples for region, tier and fallback cases.
The validator runs as a standalone binary and as a GitHub Action that fails PRs containing invalid routing config files (yaml/json) in infra/routing/.

Validator detects and rejects: circular fallbacks, mixed-precision model fallbacks that are incompatible with client SLO constraints, region->tier mismatches (e.g. premium-only model pinned to standard-only region), and private VPC-only model usages surfaced for hosted-only deployments.
Unit test coverage >= 90% for parser + validation rules, and integration tests exercising a canary routing config that demonstrates fallback behavior.
Migration guide + automated lint job to surface deprecated constructs in existing configs and provide suggested transformations.
Rollout plan with feature-flagged runtime acceptance and monitoring dashboards for invalid-policy-rate and routing-fallback-count.
No config causing undefined routing precedence should pass validation (precedence must be explicit or deterministic).
technical_notes: DSL goals: declarative, deterministic, and composable. Support selectors: region, region-group, customer_tier, model_profile, capacity_hint, and explicit fallback list with optional weights.

Prototype grammar: rule := when <selector-expr> -> route { primary: model_id, fallbacks: [model_id:weight], region_affinity: prefer|require } ; selectors support AND/OR/NOT and parentheses for precedence.

Validation rules to implement: type checking (strings/ints/enums), model-compatibility checks using model_manifest (quantization, memory_estimate, seq_len_cap), capacity constraints (region capacity tags), and security constraints (private-only models must include 'vpc=true').

Reject ambiguous precedence: if two rules have overlapping selectors and identical specificity, validator requires explicit priority or will mark as error. Add rule-uid hashing to make rule order deterministic when priority not provided, but prefer explicit priorities.
Plan to reuse existing parser lib (pegjs -> migrate to nearley/parboiled in Go) — go-validator will be written in Go to integrate with runtime and CI pipelines.
Schema evolution: include $schema-version field; validator must support backward-compatibility checks and emit upgrade suggestions.

Failure modes to detect early: circular model fallbacks (A->B->A), fallbacks that would cross-account-region restrictions, and fallbacks to models not present in the model_catalog for the target deployment type.

2026-03-10: First CI action prototype passes simple rules but flagged overlapping-selector detection as false-negative; working on specificity scoring algorithm.
